strategy.summary: Reproduce the SymPy geometry regression affecting Triangle.excenters by checking exact excenter coordinates for Triangle(Point(0,0), Point(6,0), Point(0,2)) using the project’s own test asserted via t.excenters[t.sides[i]]. The test should fail on the buggy revision 3b255faf11bc and pass on the fixed revision that includes PR #28262 changes (operator precedence in excenter coordinate formula and corrected side-length assignments).

pinned_because: No era/toolchain constraints are provided in the evidence; keep the environment close to SymPy’s pure-Python defaults so the failing geometry logic is exercised.

strategy.reproducing_test:
# Add or run the project’s test_excenters in sympy/geometry/tests/test_polygon.py
# (or cherry-pick it if it is already present in the buggy/fixed checkout)

def test_excenters():
    t = Triangle(Point(0, 0), Point(6, 0), Point(0, 2))
    assert t.excenters[t.sides[0]] == Point(sqrt(10) + 4, sqrt(10) + 4)
    assert t.excenters[t.sides[1]] == Point(2 - sqrt(10), -2 + sqrt(10))
    assert t.excenters[t.sides[2]] == Point(2 + sqrt(10), -sqrt(10) - 2)

On the fixed revision (containing PR #28262), the same assertions all pass and the test suite reports success.
